title: Constraining the Radio Emission of TRAPPIST-1
question: Does TRAPPIST-1 emit gyrosynchrotron radio emission at 44 and 97.5 GHz, and what do upper limits imply for magnetic properties and energetic proton flux at its planets?

what.value: Stellar parameters (mass, radius, Teff, Prot, B field, Lx, age, distance)

evidence.quote: Stellar Parameters of TRAPPIST-1 taken from the literature.

external_data.citation: van_groot, delrez, vida, rein_bas, wheatley, burg_mam, kane

what.value: 6 GHz upper limit of <8.1 uJy for TRAPPIST-1

recipe.method: CLEANed images from pipeline-calibrated data; 3 sigma upper limits from image RMS
Analysed individual scans (~7 min ALMA, ~4 min VLA) for flares

recipe.goal: Assess significance of NE source candidates
recipe.method: 10^4 Gaussian noise images convolved with the beam; count peaks

recipe.goal: Constrain emitting region size and proton flux
recipe.method: Gyrosynchrotron equations: region size x, electron density N, scaled to outgoing proton flux at TRAPPIST-1e
key_parameters: B = 600 G, delta = 2, d = 12.45 pc, nu = 97.5 GHz, S = 10.6 uJy
assumptions: Electron-to-proton ratio ~10^3 as in solar flares; flux scaled by R/r^2 with pi sr

evidence.quote: we place $3 \sigma$ upper flux limits of 10.6 and 16.2 $\upmu$Jy, respectively
we place $3 \sigma$ upper flux limits of 10.6 and 16.2 $\upmu$Jy, respectively
median $3 \sigma$ upper limits of 110 $\mu$Jy and 190$\mu$Jy per scan for ALMA and the VLA
the emitting region is constrained by our ALMA upper limits to $\leq 0.02~ R_J$
The resulting number density of electrons is $N \leq  5 \times 10^8~ cm^{-3}$.
We find a particle flux incident on the closest habitable planet, TRAPPIST-1e (0.02 au), to be $10^5 pfu$.
